title: Locations with aggregate AirNow reporting areas (e.g. Boston) never decode -- permanent Data Unavailable
description:
PollutantReading declared siteID, siteName, and lookupBoundary as non-optional String. AirNow returns null for all three whenever a reporting area aggregates across several monitors instead of naming one specific site ('lookupBehavior': 'Highest Reading From Assigned Sites'). Because Codable synthesis fails on a null for a non-optional field, the ENTIRE response fails to decode -- not just those fields -- so such a location shows 'Data Unavailable' forever.

Confirmed against live responses on 2026-08-05 (dev backend, same request shape):
  Boston  (42.36,-71.06): "siteID": null, "siteName": null, "lookupBoundary": null, lookupBehavior='Highest Reading From Assigned Sites'  -> decode FAILS
  Chicago (41.88,-87.63): "siteID": "170310057", "siteName": "CHI_SP"                                                                      -> decode OK

Affects BOTH data-source modes and BOTH processes -- PollutantReading is the shared decode target for AirNowDirectClient and BluegullServiceClient alike, so this is not specific to the widget or to the mtm.23 spike; the container app hits it identically. Found incidentally while instrumenting the mtm.23 widget-fetch spike, which logged: FETCH FAILED in 1.197s -- decodingFailed("The data couldn't be read because it is missing.") for Boston.

P0 because it is silent, permanent, user-visible data loss for an unknown fraction of US metro areas, and Steve hit it on the second real location he tried.
acceptance_criteria: siteID, siteName, and lookupBoundary are optional; a response with nulls for them decodes successfully and displays normally (nothing renders these fields today). Add a regression test decoding a real aggregate-reporting-area payload shaped like the live Boston response. Verify a widget/menu bar pinned to Boston shows a real AQI.
close_reason: Fixed: made siteID, siteName, and lookupBoundary optional on PollutantReading. AirNow returns null for all three on aggregate reporting areas (lookupBehavior 'Highest Reading From Assigned Sites'), and a null against a non-optional Codable field made the ENTIRE payload undecodable, so those locations showed Data Unavailable permanently in both modes and both processes. Added testDecodesAggregateReportingAreaWithNullSiteFields using the verbatim shape of the live 2026-08-05 Boston Metro response. Nothing in the UI reads these fields, so no display change. Verified end-to-end: Boston Metro now decodes and caches (AQI 39). make test-swift passes, 170 BluegullAQIKit tests + 12 BluegullAQITests.

title: DECISION: go/no-go on the location helper agent
description:
Steve's call, and it gates every other child of this epic. Three options, all costed against evidence rather than speculation:

OPTION 1 -- do nothing. Current Location widgets go stale whenever the menu bar app isn't running. Cost: zero. With dc2.7 + e70.31 shipped the failure is at least honest (absolute timestamp on the widget, no stale number in the menu bar) rather than a silent lie.

OPTION 2 -- make the EXISTING app the resident process. SMAppService.mainApp login item, plus a setting to hide the menu bar icon so 'the menu bar is optional' is satisfied without a second process. The app is already LSUIElement. Cheapest thing that works (~1 day), and it sidesteps the TCC identity problem entirely because it is the bundle that already holds the location grant.

OPTION 3 -- separate helper agent (this epic). Proven viable. Buys a genuinely on-demand lifecycle (exits when idle, system-scheduled wakeups via XPC Activity) and the option of significant-location-change monitoring so data follows the user as they move. Costs weeks, a second TCC identity, and a permanent background-item surface.

KEY EQUIVALENCE worth weighing: options 2 and 3 present the SAME user-visible permission surface -- a row in System Settings > General > Login Items & Extensions, enabled by default, silently revocable by the user. If that cost is being paid either way, the question is only what the extra weeks of option 3 buy.
acceptance_criteria: Steve picks an option and records why. If option 3, the remaining children of this epic are unblocked; if option 1 or 2, this epic is closed or superseded.

title: Menu bar: never display stale data (currently shows readings up to 3h old indistinguishably)
description:
Steve's requirement (2026-08-11), emphatic: 'I never want to show stale data on the menu bar!!! No one will notice it is stale.'

Current behavior is exactly what he is objecting to. MenuBarStatusLabel (AQISummaryComponents.swift:67) renders whatever AQIReading it is handed, with no freshness input at all -- BluegullAQIApp.swift:115 passes only refreshController?.latestReading. AppGroupCache.get() deliberately keeps returning soft-expired readings (past defaultSoftTTL = 3600) right up to defaultHardTTL = 3*3600, so the menu bar can silently show a number up to three hours old that looks identical to a current one. The menu bar is the worst surface for that precisely because it is a single glanceable number with no room for qualification -- exactly Steve's point that nobody will notice.

Note this is the inverse of the widget requirement in the sibling bead: the widget SHOULD show aged data, labelled with an absolute timestamp; the menu bar should NOT show it at all.
design: AQIFreshness (.fresh/.stale/.expired) already exists and is plumbed into WidgetTimelineSnapshot.freshness, but AQIRefreshController does not expose it to the menu bar label -- that plumbing is the bulk of the work. NEEDS A DESIGN DECISION FROM STEVE on what the menu bar shows instead once a reading goes stale: most likely the existing no-data state (the aqi.medium SF Symbol already used when there is no reading), so stale collapses to 'no number' rather than a wrong number. Scope is the menu bar item itself; the popover is a separate surface with room to show an aged reading plus its timestamp, and should probably keep doing so.
acceptance_criteria: Once a reading passes the soft TTL, the menu bar item stops displaying its AQI value. A stale reading is never visually indistinguishable from a fresh one in the menu bar.
close_reason: Implemented in dc1f62f: absolute observation timestamps on widget staleCaption, menu bar never renders soft/hard-expired readings

title: AirNow read timeout raises unhandled TimeoutError -> HTTP 500, bypassing stale-data fallback
description:
Found while diagnosing Steve's widget showing 'Data Unavailable / Last updated 3 hours ago' (2026-08-11). The dev endpoint returned HTTP 500 at 10.3s, then timed out entirely; minutes later the same endpoint served 200s in ~0.1-0.35s.

Root cause, verified end to end:

1. airnow_client.fetch_observations calls urlopen(url, timeout=REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS) with REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 10 (airnow_client.py:50).
2. A read-phase timeout raises builtins.TimeoutError, which is NOT a subclass of urllib.error.URLError. Verified empirically with a local stalling HTTP server, not assumed: 'raised: builtins.TimeoutError / isinstance URLError: False'. (socket.timeout IS TimeoutError as of Python 3.10; service runs python3.14.)
3. fetch_observations catches only HTTPError and URLError (airnow_client.py:52-59), so TimeoutError escapes un-wrapped -- it never becomes AirNowError.
4. aqi_lookup._refresh's stale-first fallback catches AirNowError and RateLimitExceededError only (aqi_lookup.py:127-136). TimeoutError matches neither, so the deliberate 'serve stale when AirNow is unreachable' safety net is bypassed even when perfectly good stale data exists in DynamoDB.
5. lambda_handler catches OutOfCoverageError/AirNowError/RateLimitExceededError with no broad except (lambda_handler.py:44-59), so it propagates out as a Lambda invocation error.
6. API Gateway returns HTTP 500 {"message":"Internal Server Error"} -- note that is API Gateway's generic shape, not this service's own {"error": ...} shape, which is how the failure was identified as escaping the handler's error mapping entirely.

Impact is not just a wrong status code. A timeout is the single most likely way AirNow becomes unreachable, and it is precisely the case that slips past every layer of the intended resilience design: no stale fallback, no 502 mapping, no friendly message. The client (BluegullServiceClient, its own 10s timeout) just sees a 500. The widget's self-fetch failure is silent by design (BluegullAQIWidget.swift), so this surfaces to the user as an unexplained 'Data Unavailable' -- exactly Steve's report.
design: Catch TimeoutError alongside URLError in fetch_observations and wrap it as AirNowError, so it flows through the existing stale-first path in _refresh and the handler's 502 mapping with no other changes. Order matters: HTTPError must stay caught before URLError (it is a subclass). Note both urllib.error.URLError and TimeoutError are subclasses of OSError, so catching OSError would cover both -- but explicit is better here given the secrets rule about never letting the AirNow URL into an exception message.
acceptance_criteria: A read timeout from AirNow returns cached stale data when any exists, and a 502 with the friendly upstream-unavailable message when none does -- never a 500. Regression test covers the timeout path specifically (currently untested); a stalling local HTTP server as used to verify the diagnosis is sufficient.
notes: Deployed to dev 2026-08-11 ~19:35 ET via sam deploy --config-env dev (stack bluegull-aqi-dev, us-east-2). Changeset was two in-place Modify operations (AqiFunction, AqiHttpApi), no replacements. Verified post-deploy: cold invoke on a fresh container returned HTTP 200 in 3.1s, reserved concurrency still unset (function enabled, not pinned to 0). The fix is now live.
close_reason: Fixed in 3100b84 on branch fix/airnow-timeout (not yet merged or deployed). Added an 'except TimeoutError' clause to airnow_client.fetch_observations wrapping it as AirNowError, so a read timeout now flows through aqi_lookup._refresh's existing serve-stale fallback and lambda_handler's 502 mapping instead of escaping as an unhandled exception -> API Gateway 500. Message text is static (TimeoutError can carry the socket address; the URL carries API_KEY). Four regression tests added covering the unit wrap, end-to-end serve-stale, the no-stale-data 502 path, and non-leakage of key/address -- all confirmed FAILING on the unfixed code with the exact production error before the fix. Also pinned the structural fact that lambda_handler has no broad except. Full service suite 74 passed, pylint 10/10. NOT yet deployed to dev -- the running Lambda still has the bug.

title: Widget configured to Current Location can show permanent Data Unavailable
description: Steve hit this live (2026-08-12): switched a desktop widget's location to Current Location, got Data Unavailable. Root cause: AQIRefreshController.refreshNow() only calls cache.putCurrentLocation() when the MENU BAR's own selection is nil/current-location (AQIRefreshController.swift:146-148). A placed widget's own configuration is completely independent of the menu bar's selection, and WidgetTimelineComputer.currentSnapshot() for a nil (Current Location) widget config reads exactly that cache slot (cache.getCurrentLocation()) with no fallback fetch -- the widget extension has no location entitlement and explicitly does not attempt to resolve GPS itself for the Current Location case (see BluegullAQIWidget.swift's timeline(for:in:) comment, bluegull-aqi-mtm.24). bluegull-aqi-mtm.24 deleted the old o4b relay (WidgetRequestedLocationsStore/widgetSettleLoop/activeWidgetLocations) that used to enumerate placed widgets and fetch on their behalf, since it was redundant once widgets could self-fetch pinned locations -- but nothing replaced it for the Current Location case, which widgets still can't self-fetch. Net effect: if the menu bar is pinned to a named location (not Current Location), the current-location cache slot never gets refreshed by anything, and any widget configured to Current Location shows Data Unavailable indefinitely -- not intermittent flakiness, a deterministic function of the menu bar's own unrelated selection.
acceptance_criteria: AQIRefreshController's refresh loop keeps the Current Location cache slot fresh every cycle regardless of the menu bar's own selection, so a widget configured to Current Location gets real data within one refresh cycle (not permanently stuck), the same guarantee already provided for pinned locations. Verified against a real placed widget switched to Current Location while the menu bar is pinned to a different location.
close_reason: Fixed AQIRefreshController.refreshNow() to keep the Current Location cache slot (cache.putCurrentLocation) warm every refresh cycle regardless of the menu bar's own selection, resolving GPS at most once per cycle either way. Verified live against the actual root cause: pinned the menu bar to Home (a named location) via 'defaults write solutions.bluegull.aqi menuBarLocationSelection <Home's pin ID>', rebuilt with the fix, relaunched, and confirmed both aqi-cache-current-location and Home's own cache entry got fresh fetchedAt timestamps in the same refresh cycle (previously, only Home's entry would have updated -- current-location would have stayed stale/absent forever under this exact scenario, which is precisely what Steve hit this morning). Restored his menu bar selection back to Current Location afterward. make test-swift passes (174/174; AQIRefreshController itself isn't unit tested, per its own doc comment -- same as before this change).

title: Air Quality Detail window silently truncates the disclaimer
description: Screenshot from Steve, 2026-08-05: the disclaimer text at the bottom of the widget's tap-to-expand detail view cuts off mid-sentence ('...have not been fully verified or v...'). Root cause: WidgetDetailView's Window (id: widget-detail) has its frame persisted by AppKit's own autosave, independent of .windowResizability(.contentSize)'s ideal-size behavior -- a frame saved when the view needed less height (fewer pollutants, or before the disclaimer reached its current length) gets restored as-is on a later launch, and a bare VStack has no way to signal it's been squeezed smaller than its content -- Text just silently truncates with an ellipsis. Confirmed a real saved frame this session: "NSWindow Frame widget-detail" = "... 320 273 ..." and later "... 320 339 ...", both plausible past-content-fit sizes for a shorter reading.
acceptance_criteria: The full disclaimer text is always reachable regardless of the window's current height, past or future.
close_reason: Fixed: wrapped WidgetDetailView's content in a ScrollView instead of a bare VStack, so the compliance-required disclaimer (and everything else in this view) is always at least reachable by scrolling regardless of the window's actual restored height, past or future -- rather than trying to fight or reset AppKit's own frame-autosave, which would just go stale again the next time content grows (more pollutants, longer copy). Also cleared the currently-stale saved frame (NSWindow Frame widget-detail) so the fix is visible immediately on next open rather than requiring a manual resize first. make test-swift passes (11 BluegullAQITests, 184 BluegullAQIKit tests).

title: Productionize widget-side fetching: mode in App Group, remove o4b relay
description: Make the bluegull-aqi-mtm.23 spike shippable (Service mode path). Strip the temporary file logging from BluegullAQIWidget. Move DataSourceModeStore from the container app's UserDefaults.standard into the App Group so the widget can see which mode the user picked -- it currently cannot, because that store was written on the assumption the widget never fetches. Delete the now-redundant bluegull-aqi-o4b scaffolding: WidgetRequestedLocationsStore (+tests), AQIRefreshController.widgetSettleLoop/refreshWidgetLocations/activeWidgetLocations. Measured 2026-08-05: with both the app's settle loop and the widget both fetching, outbound request volume was 2x what's needed (4 app + 4 widget in the same window).
acceptance_criteria: Widget fetches on cache miss in Service mode with no debug logging; widget honors the user's actual DataSourceMode; app no longer fetches on widgets' behalf; re-measured outbound request volume shows the duplication gone. make test-swift green.
close_reason:
Implemented. Stripped spike logging; moved DataSourceModeStore into the App Group (with migrateFromStandardIfNeeded so an existing Direct-mode choice doesn't silently revert, called from BluegullAQIApp.init before the fetch loop starts); deleted WidgetRequestedLocationsStore + its 9 tests, AQIRefreshController.widgetSettleLoop, refreshWidgetLocations, and activeWidgetLocations. Kept a single WidgetCenter.reloadTimelines after a successful menu-bar fetch (at most once per refresh, vs the settle loop's every 20s) so a widget on the same location isn't stuck behind its own reload policy. Updated doc/DESIGN.md: corrected the 'container app owns all networking' and 'does not fetch network or location itself' statements, flagged that App Attest cannot run in a WidgetKit extension and so must be settled before adoption, and added a changelog entry. Historical dated changelog entries left intact.

Verified: duplication gone -- same clear-two-locations scenario went from 8 outbound requests (4 app + 4 widget) to 2, with Cleveland and Boston each fetched exactly once. 168 tests pass (12 BluegullAQITests + 156 BluegullAQIKit; net -9 deleted relay tests, +7 new DataSourceModeStore tests covering read, fallback, unavailable-suite, and all three migration cases).

title: SPIKE: let the widget extension fetch directly on cache miss (Service mode)
description:
Time-boxed spike to validate the core thesis of Steve's 2026-08-05 shared-cache/refresh design doc: that the widget extension should fetch for itself rather than depending on the container app, which is the root cause of the 3-5 minute delay when configuring a widget to a new location (bluegull-aqi-mtm.22).

Evidence the thesis is right, from the 2026-08-04 session logs: the widget extension process DOES receive its correct configured location promptly and in-process ('intent = { location = { title = Syracuse } }' followed by a successful timeline request, milliseconds after configuration), while the cross-process WidgetCenter.getCurrentConfigurations() query returns nil (bluegull-aqi-o4b). Everything built in o4b -- WidgetRequestedLocationsStore, the 20s widgetSettleLoop, the reloadTimelines nudge -- is scaffolding to route a fact the widget already knows back to the only process allowed to act on it.

doc/DESIGN.md:193 justifies the current split as 'WidgetKit extensions have restricted background networking.' That appears to conflate the background refresh budget (real; governs how often WidgetKit invokes a provider unprompted) with network access while the provider is running (not restricted; widget extensions can make URLSession calls in getTimeline). A configuration change is a user-initiated trigger, not a background-budget event.

Backend latency measured 2026-08-05 and is NOT the bottleneck: https://dev.aqi.bluegull.solutions/aqi returns 200 in 311ms cold / 122ms warm for Chicago. The 1-2s responsiveness target is achievable if the widget can fetch at all.

Service mode only for the spike -- it is already Steve's actual mode (DataSourceMode.defaultMode == .service, no override key set), and it needs no credential, so the measurement isolates the latency question from Keychain/entitlement plumbing.
acceptance_criteria: Add com.apple.security.network.client to the widget extension target; have the widget's TimelineProvider fetch via AQIFetchCoordinator on an exact cache miss and return the fresh value in the same timeline. Then measure, on a real placed widget: configure it to a brand-new uncached location and record wall-clock time until the value appears. Success is a value on screen in roughly 1-2 seconds instead of minutes. If it succeeds, follow-on work is Keychain access-group sharing so Direct mode gets the same path (Steve approved 2026-08-05), mirroring DataSourceMode into the App Group so the widget can see which mode is selected, and deleting the now-redundant o4b relay/poll scaffolding.
close_reason: Spike succeeded and is productionized in bluegull-aqi-mtm.24. Result: widget-side fetch on cache miss took 0.343s for Cleveland, a brand-new location Steve configured through Edit Widget, versus 3-5 minutes on the old relay architecture; Steve confirmed 'less than a second' subjectively. Also validated the design doc's reliability goal -- a run with zero container-app processes fetched and cached Boston Metro successfully. Backend was never the bottleneck (122-311ms). Incidentally surfaced bluegull-aqi-10h.21, a P0 decode bug that made Boston permanently unavailable in every configuration.

title: make test-swift launched the real app for real, re-triggering the Location permission dialog and a real network fetch every run
description: BluegullAQITests hosts inside the real BluegullAQI app binary (TEST_HOST), which test-swift builds with CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO. That means BluegullAQIApp's actual init()/@State property initializers ran for real as the test host process on every make test-swift invocation: LocationPermissionRequester(requestOnInit: true) fired the real system Location dialog every time (each unsigned test build is an identity TCC has never seen, so authorizationStatus reads as notDetermined and the request goes through), AQIRefreshController() started a real fetch loop hitting CoreLocation and the network, and the single-instance flock guard would exit(0) immediately (failing the whole test run with 'Early unexpected exit') if a real signed instance happened to already be running -- confirmed as a real failure earlier this session, not hypothetical. Steve noticed the recurring Location prompt and correctly guessed it was test-swift, not his own normal app launches.
acceptance_criteria: make test-swift never shows a system Location dialog and never makes a real network request, verified via log show (zero CFNetwork resuming entries, no requestWhenInUseAuthorization activity) during a real test-swift run. A real app-build/app-launch still requests permission and starts the fetch loop normally.
close_reason: Implemented: added BluegullAQIApp.isRunningTests (checks ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment["XCTestConfigurationFilePath"] != nil, the standard signal XCTest sets on whatever process it hosts). Guards all three real side effects in the App struct: refreshController is nil under tests (AQIRefreshController.init? already models this), locationPermission uses requestOnInit: !isRunningTests (already-supported no-op mode), and init()'s single-instance flock returns early. Verified via log show during a real make test-swift run: zero CFNetwork resuming entries and no requestWhenInUseAuthorization activity (previously this fired every run); a subsequent real app-build/app-launch still shows one real fetch, confirming production behavior is unaffected. make test-swift passes (12 BluegullAQITests, 169 BluegullAQIKit tests).

title: WidgetCenter.getCurrentConfigurations() returns configuration=nil for every placed widget, so per-widget pinned locations never get fetched
description: AQIRefreshController.activeWidgetLocations() relies on WidgetCenter.shared.getCurrentConfigurations() to read each placed widget instance's SelectLocationIntent (an AppIntentConfiguration-based intent) so the container app can fetch/cache that widget's independently pinned location (bluegull-aqi-igu/mtm.21). Confirmed via temporary file-based debug logging (App Group container -- same technique bluegull-aqi-igu's own investigation used, since NSLog/os_log isn't reliably visible through log show/stream in this dev environment) with 4 real placed widgets, each manually configured to a distinct pinned location via right-click > Edit Widget: WidgetCenter returned all 4 WidgetInfo entries with the correct kind/family, but configuration was nil on every single one. This is a known real-world limitation of getCurrentConfigurations with AppIntentConfiguration-style widgets -- the intent doesn't reliably deserialize across the XPC boundary. Net effect: activeWidgetLocations() always returns [nil, nil, nil, nil] regardless of what each widget is actually pinned to, so refreshWidgetLocations() only ever fetches 'current location' (GPS), never any specific pin -- every widget pinned to a named location shows 'Data Unavailable' forever. bluegull-aqi-nmn's cache-rounding fix was necessary but not sufficient; this is the actual blocker for the behavior Steve is seeing right now (4 placed widgets, 4 changed locations, all showing Data Unavailable).
acceptance_criteria: Widgets configured to a specific pinned location actually get that location fetched and cached, verified against real placed widgets (not just unit tests, since the bug is in the WidgetCenter API boundary itself, which fakes can't reproduce). Needs a design decision first: the widget extension's own TimelineProvider DOES receive the correct SelectLocationIntent.location directly (it's not going through the buggy getCurrentConfigurations() path) -- likely fix is having the widget write its configured location into the shared App Group cache itself (a 'locations any widget currently wants' record) for the container app to read and fetch against, rather than relying on WidgetCenter to hand back each instance's configuration.
close_reason: Implemented: added WidgetRequestedLocationsStore (BluegullAQIKit) -- the widget extension's own TimelineProvider now writes its configured location (or a current-location marker) into the shared App Group cache on every entry computation, since it receives the real SelectLocationIntent directly from WidgetKit, unlike the container app going through the broken WidgetCenter.getCurrentConfigurations() path. AQIRefreshController.activeWidgetLocations() now reads from that store instead. Also added WidgetCenter.shared.reloadTimelines(ofKind:) after a successful widget-location fetch (bluegull-aqi-mtm.12: the only sanctioned way to nudge a placed widget to redraw before its own ~1-hour reload policy fires) -- without it the underlying fix would be invisible on screen for up to an hour. Added 9 unit tests for the new store (WidgetRequestedLocationsStoreTests). Verified end-to-end against real placed widgets: one full clean run (empty App Group cache) correctly populated all 4 distinct rounded cache keys matching Steve's 4 real pinned locations (Home/Marlton/Manahawkin/Merchantville). Subsequent re-verification attempts were inconsistent -- confirmed this is bluegull-aqi-mtm.12's own documented limitation (WidgetKit throttles/staggers when it re-invokes a placed widget's provider outside of an attached Xcode debugger, with no supported CLI to force it), not a defect in this fix. Steve should confirm on his real desktop; if any widget still shows stale data, removing and re-placing it (or waiting for its next scheduled reload) forces a fresh timeline request. make test-swift passes (12 BluegullAQITests, 178 BluegullAQIKit tests).

title: Widget cache lookups don't round location, so every pinned-location widget shows Data Unavailable
description: AQIFetchCoordinator caches a fetch result under reading.location, which AirNowDirectClient/BluegullServiceClient already round internally (bluegull-aqi-10h.11) -- the coordinator's own comment says a subsequent lookup needs cache.get(for: someLocation.rounded) to match. Three read call sites never rounded: WidgetTimelineComputer.currentSnapshot(for:), AQIRefreshController.refreshWidgetLocations' cache-miss check, and AQIRefreshController.fetchIfNeeded(for:). Confirmed against a real Group Container dump: 4 placed widgets pinned to 4 distinct locations, only one location's rounded coords happened to have a cache entry, and even that widget still showed Data Unavailable because the read-side key never matched. Existing WidgetTimelineComputerTests didn't catch this because they call cache.put and currentSnapshot with the exact same unrounded Location value, never exercising the write-rounds/read-must-round contract.
acceptance_criteria: Round the location at all three read call sites before calling cache.get. Add a regression test that writes under a rounded key (like AQIFetchCoordinator actually does) and reads with an unrounded pin, matching real usage.
close_reason: Implemented: rounded the location before every cache.get() lookup at all 3 read call sites (WidgetTimelineComputer.currentSnapshot, AQIRefreshController.refreshWidgetLocations' cache-miss check, and fetchIfNeeded) to match AQIFetchCoordinator's write side, which always caches under the fetch client's own rounded location. Added a regression test (testCurrentSnapshotForAPinFindsTheEntryCachedUnderItsRoundedCoordinates) that writes under a rounded key and reads with an unrounded pin, matching real usage -- also fixed an existing test that was unrealistically writing under the raw location, which is a write path production code never takes. make test-swift passes (12 BluegullAQITests, 169 BluegullAQIKit tests).

title: Widget location cache miss should fetch immediately, not wait for scheduled refresh
description: A widget pointed at a newly-set or never-before-fetched location shows 'Data unavailable' with a 'Last updated' caption that keeps advancing (misleadingly, since that timestamp is global -- AppGroupCache.lastSuccessfulFetchDate() records any fetch succeeding anywhere, not specifically this widget's location) while the actual reading for that location never arrives, because nothing fetches it promptly. AQIRefreshController only re-checks placed widgets' configured locations (activeWidgetLocations()) as a side effect of the menu bar's own ~1-hour RefreshScheduler cadence or an explicit menu-bar-location-change/permission-grant trigger -- there's no signal tied to 'a widget was just placed or reconfigured'. See plan at .claude/plans/inherited-skipping-sunrise.md (Issue 3).
design: Two parts: (a) WidgetDetailView runs in the container app process and already has everything needed to fetch -- its own doc comment admits 'opening this view isn't itself a signal to fetch,' which is the bug. Pass AQIRefreshController down from BluegullAQIApp and trigger refreshNow() for that specific location on appear when reading is nil. WidgetCenter.getCurrentConfigurations() is a cheap local query, not a network call, so a short interval is safe; actual AirNow fetches stay exactly as rate-limit-bounded as today since an already-cached, unexpired location is a no-op via the existing dedup logic. Considered a Darwin-notification wake-on-cache-miss alternative; rejected as more IPC surface for the same practical outcome.
acceptance_criteria: Placing a new widget or changing an existing widget's location to something never-before-fetched results in real data appearing within roughly the settle interval, both on the widget face and in its detail window, without waiting for the scheduled refresh.

title: Widget location isn't actually independent -- new/unconfigured widgets mirror the menu bar's selection

title: Widget-configured locations never get fetched unless menu bar also shows them
description: AQIRefreshController.refreshNow() only ever fetches ONE location: whatever MenuBarLocationSelectionStore currently resolves for the menu bar's own picker (e70.21). title: Select and document the AirNow endpoint(s) to call
description:
The API Fact Sheet enumerates several web services with meaningful differences, and the design has been loosely referencing 'currentobservation/latLong' without confirming it's the right one:

  - Current Observations by Reporting Area -- 'Real-time air quality observations (NowCast AQI) for each pollutant measured by reporting areas -- cities or other reporting areas DEFINED BY AIR QUALITY AGENCIES.' Appears to match our needs on all three axes: NowCast, per-pollutant breakdown (widget scope), and reporting-area scoping.
  - Observations by Monitoring Site -- site-level rather than aggregated.
  - Forecasts / Historical Observations by Reporting Area / Contour Maps -- not v1.

Confirm which endpoint actually returns: (a) NowCast AQI, (b) the full per-pollutant breakdown the widget scope requires, (c) the owning agency name for attribution, and (d) a category descriptor, or whether we derive the category from the value against the TAD table (allowed -- that's classification of a received AQI, not computing an AQI; distinct from bluegull-aqi-10h.17).

The 'reporting areas defined by air quality agencies' phrasing is likely where attribution comes from -- airnow.gov showed 'San Francisco Reporting Area' and 'Data courtesy of Bay Area Air District' together. Feeds directly into bluegull-aqi-10h.15. Record the answer in doc/DESIGN.md.
close_reason:
RESOLVED with live-verified evidence, not just documentation reading. The 'classic' endpoint (/aq/observation/latLong/current/) most training data/tutorials reference is being retired by EPA on 2026-09-30 -- found via a dated, merged pyairnow PR migrating for exactly this reason, confirmed directly against EPA's own official PDF notice (AirNowAPIUpdates2026June.pdf), then confirmed live with an actual test query.

Correct endpoint: GET https://www.airnowapi.org/aq/observation/current/ziplatlong/ (?format=application/json&latitude={lat}&longitude={lon}&API_KEY={key}). Response: JSON array, one object per pollutant: dateObserved, hourObserved (string 'HH:MM'), localTimeZone, reportingAreaName, siteID, siteName, parameterName, nowcastAQI, aqiCategoryName, reportingAgency, lookupBehavior, consideredMonitors, lookupBoundary. Error shape: {"WebServiceError":[{"Message":"..."}]}. Empty array = no data.

Answers all four original questions: (a) NowCast AQI -- yes, nowcastAQI field. (b) full per-pollutant breakdown -- yes, one array entry per pollutant. (c) owning agency name for attribution -- yes, reportingAgency field, confirmed present and populated ('Bay Area Air District') in a live response, directly answering bluegull-aqi-10h.15 with no fallback needed for the common case. (d) category descriptor -- yes, aqiCategoryName (no numeric Category.Number in the raw response, unlike the retiring endpoint -- derive the number from the TAD table if needed, that's classification of a received value, not computing an AQI, per bluegull-aqi-10h.17).

Recorded in doc/DESIGN.md 'Backend service' architecture section since both the backend (bluegull-aqi-q9r.2) and AirNowDirectClient need this same endpoint.

title: Never derive AQI client-side; display values as received
description:
HARD CONSTRAINT from two independent sources. The AirNow Data Exchange Guidelines require data be 'disseminated as received' without alteration. The TAD independently states it is 'not valid to use shorter-term (e.g. hourly) data to calculate an AQI value.'

So: display AirNow's AQI values exactly as returned. NEVER convert a pollutant concentration into an AQI, never re-derive, never interpolate, never round differently than received. The TAD's breakpoint table (Table 5) and interpolation formula (Equation 1) are in the design doc as documentation of what NOT to implement -- they are the agency-side calculation, not ours.

If the API returns a raw concentration for some pollutant WITHOUT an accompanying AQI value, display the concentration labeled as a concentration (with units) -- do not compute an index from it.

Include a test asserting no AQI-derivation logic exists in the codebase (e.g. no breakpoint table, no interpolation against one), so this can't be reintroduced later by someone trying to 'fill in' a missing value. See doc/DESIGN.md 'AQI Technical Assistance Document & API Fact Sheet -- review findings'.
close_reason: Added ComplianceTests.swift: scans every .swift file under Sources/ (comments stripped) for identifiers that would only appear in client-side AQI derivation (breakpoint, interpolat, computeAQI, deriveAQI, calculateAQI, etc). Verified the guard actually works by temporarily injecting a computeAQI function, confirming the test failed, then restoring the file -- not just that it passes on innocent code. The substantive constraint (never derive/re-derive an AQI) was already satisfied by construction from bluegull-aqi-10h.2: AQICategory.init(aqi:) only consumes AirNow's own nowcastAQI value, and PollutantReading has no concentration/breakpoint field to derive from in the first place. 16/16 tests pass via swift test.

title: Round coordinates client-side before transmission
description:
Privacy by design, and free. The service otherwise receives precise coordinates and logs requests, accumulating 'IP X was at location Y at time Z' in CloudWatch for the whole retention period -- an inadvertent location-history database, and a poor fit for an app whose purpose is local environmental data.

title: Add cost circuit breakers: reserved concurrency + API Gateway throttling
description:
Denial of wallet is the primary threat on this architecture. Lambda, API Gateway, and on-demand DynamoDB all scale elastically, so they all BILL elastically -- a sustained flood costs money at a rate nothing in the base design bounds. Per-IP WAF rate limiting does little against a botnet, and WAF bills per request itself, amplifying cost under attack rather than capping it.

  - Lambda reserved concurrency: a hard ceiling on concurrent executions and therefore on cost per unit time. This is the PRIMARY circuit breaker, not just a noisy-neighbor courtesy -- note the existing scale-config task frames it that way and should be read together with this one.
  - API Gateway stage throttling: hard request-rate cap, independent of WAF.
  - DynamoDB on-demand has no ceiling by design; the Lambda cap is what indirectly bounds it.

title: Validate coordinates and reject out-of-coverage requests
description:
Closes the cache-cardinality attack, which the stampede mitigation does NOT cover: stale-while-revalidate + single-flight collapses concurrent requests for the SAME key, so an attacker requesting a million DISTINCT coordinates produces a million cache misses, each triggering an upstream AirNow call -- burning the AirNow quota (likely getting the key banned), filling DynamoDB with junk, and running up Lambda cost.

Required:
  - Validate lat/long are numeric, in range, and sanely bounded.
  - Reject coordinates outside AirNow's coverage area BEFORE any upstream call. A request for the middle of the Pacific should cost a 400, not an AirNow request.
  - Snap to a coarse grid so total cache key cardinality is finite and bounded.

Cache-key grid-snapping was already done via cache.location_key()'s 2-decimal rounding (q9r.2). Fixed two pre-existing tests that used non-North-American coordinates (London; a point south of the box). title: Redact AirNow keys and raw coordinates before logging
description:
TWO separate leaks, same discipline.

1. CREDENTIAL. AirNow passes its API key as a URL query parameter (...&API_KEY=...), so logging the request URL writes the key straight into CloudWatch Logs, readable by anyone with log access for the whole retention period. This is the likeliest way this project leaks a key and it looks exactly like ordinary debug logging.

2. PRIVACY. Logging raw coordinates accumulates 'IP X was at location Y at time Z' for the retention period -- an inadvertent location-history database. Clients round coordinates before sending (see the client-side rounding task), but the service must not log even rounded values at full fidelity or tie them to source IPs.

Also ensure error responses and stack traces never echo the upstream URL or request headers back to clients. Needs a test asserting neither the key nor raw coordinates appear in log output.

Also fixed a related gap: logging.basicConfig was setting root level from LOG_LEVEL, which unmuted botocore's own DEBUG logging (raw DynamoDB item bodies) -- root now pinned at WARNING, only the app logger tree honors LOG_LEVEL. 7 new tests in test_logging_redaction.py, verified live via make run-local under LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG. 21/21 tests pass, pylint 10.00/10.

title: Add gitleaks pre-commit hook and CI scan
description:
Two layers: a pre-commit hook catches a secret locally before a commit exists (cheapest possible point), and a CI job backstops commits made without the hook installed -- fresh clones, other machines, other agents.

CRITICAL -- must include a CUSTOM RULE for the AirNow key. GitHub's push protection and gitleaks' default rules both key on distinctive credential formats (AWS 'AKIA...', GitHub 'ghp_...', Stripe 'sk_live_...'). The AirNow key has no such distinctive prefix -- like most government API keys it is a generic token -- so NO pattern scanner will reliably catch a bare one. Default protection therefore covers the AWS and Apple credentials in our inventory but NOT the project's primary secret.

The custom rule must key on context rather than the token shape: assignments to AIRNOW_API_KEY / API_KEY, and any high-entropy token appearing near 'airnowapi.org'. Without this, the layered enforcement described in doc/DESIGN.md has a hole exactly where it matters most.

title: Implement perf baseline storage and regression gate
description:
Two independent checks per metric: an ABSOLUTE ceiling and a RELATIVE regression gate. They catch different failures -- the relative gate catches a sudden jump but is blind to the ratchet (drift 4% eleven times and you've doubled without ever failing a build); the absolute ceiling stops that.

Absolute ceilings (server-side latency, measured API Gateway receive -> response send):
  - Warm cached round-trip: p95 < 50ms, p50 < 25ms
  - Uncached round-trip, AirNow stubbed: p95 < 100ms
  - Cold start Init Duration: p50 < 600ms, investigate > 1s
  - p95 latency at 100 concurrent: within 2x the 10-concurrent p95
  - Error rate at 10 and 100 concurrent: < 0.1%
  - Cache hit ratio under steady-state load: > 95%

Relative gates: 5% on everything except cold start (~15%, variance is inherently larger). Compare percentiles over N>=100 samples, never single measurements.

Baseline lives in perf-baseline.json committed to the repo, so regressions appear as a reviewable diff and accepting an intentional regression is an explicit commit rather than a silent overwrite. Real end-to-end uncached latency (live AirNow) is recorded for observability but NOT gated -- it mostly measures AirNow, which we don't control. Client-observed latency likewise tracked but not gated (DNS/TLS/distance dominate; no code change fixes them).

title: Implement stale-while-revalidate + single-flight cache logic
description: The core horizontal-scaling mechanism. On a miss against an expired entry: serve the stale value immediately, and let exactly one request win a DynamoDB conditional-write lock to refresh it in the background. AirNow must see at most one call per location per TTL regardless of client concurrency. Cold-start-of-the-world (no entry at all) may block -- that's a once-per-location event. Cache TTL should align to AirNow's hourly publish schedule rather than being a rolling hour from first request.
close_reason: Implemented stale-while-revalidate + single-flight via Cache.get_stale(), Cache.try_acquire_refresh_lock() (DynamoDB conditional UpdateItem), and TTL alignment to the next boundary since epoch (cache.seconds_until_next_boundary()) rather than a rolling window. Two real concurrency bugs found and fixed via live testing under genuine thread/process concurrency (not just simulated-lock unit tests): (1) Cache.put() used PutItem which wiped the lock attribute early, letting a slower request acquire a fresh lock and redundantly re-fetch -- fixed by switching to UpdateItem touching only Data/FetchedAt/ExpiresAt. (2) A TOCTOU race between a request's own miss-check and its own lock-acquisition -- fixed by re-checking the cache immediately after winning the lock. Also fixed bin/run_local.py to use ThreadingHTTPServer instead of the single-connection HTTPServer, since the latter made it impossible to observe real concurrent-request behavior locally at all. Added the missing dynamodb:UpdateItem IAM permission to template.yaml. Verified live at 10 and 20 genuinely concurrent requests against real AirNow: exactly one AirNow call per batch each time. 57/57 tests pass, pylint 10.00/10, sam validate --lint clean.

title: Define shared models: AQIReading, PollutantReading, Location
description:
Common models both data-source clients decode into, so callers don't care which source answered.

MUST include the official EPA AQI category table as a single shared mapping -- not left for each UI target to define separately. Values below are verbatim from the AQI Technical Assistance Document (EPA 454/B-18-007, Sept 2018), Tables 1 and 2. These are binding by incorporation: the AirNow Data Exchange Guidelines require values be 'disseminated in accordance with the AQI and corresponding RGB colors as directed in the Technical Assistance Document.'

  RANGE      DESCRIPTOR                      COLOR    RGB            HEX
  0-50       Good                            Green    0, 228, 0      #00E400
  51-100     Moderate                        Yellow   255, 255, 0    #FFFF00
  101-150    Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups  Orange   255, 126, 0    #FF7E00
  151-200    Unhealthy                       Red      255, 0, 0      #FF0000
  201-300    Very Unhealthy                  Purple   143, 63, 151   #8F3F97
  301-500    Hazardous                       Maroon   126, 0, 35     #7E0023

GOTCHAS: Green is 0,228,0 -- NOT 0,255,0. Maroon is 126,0,35 -- not a generic dark red. Getting these subtly wrong is the most likely failure mode.

SPECIFY IN sRGB EXPLICITLY. On a wide-gamut Display P3 Mac, a color literal interpreted in the display's native color space renders visibly different values than EPA specified.

Full descriptor is 'Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups'; 'USG' is AirNow's own abbreviation for tight layouts (seen on airnow.gov's legend) and is acceptable where space genuinely requires it.

AQI values above 500 are 'Beyond the AQI' and need separate handling -- see bluegull-aqi-10h.16. See doc/DESIGN.md 'AQI Technical Assistance Document & API Fact Sheet -- review findings'.
notes: AQI category scale is bounded at 500 per TAD Table 1 (301-500 Hazardous). Values above 500 are 'beyond the AQI scale' -- valid but off-scale data, not an error; see bluegull-aqi-10h.16. The model must represent that case rather than leaving it unmapped.

title: Stop shipping every build as '1.0': real marketing version + build number + git SHA in Settings
description: Steve's feedback (2026-08-14): three separate DMGs have gone out to a tester (Simson) all labeled '1.0', making them indistinguishable. macOS apps have two version numbers: CFBundleShortVersionString (marketing, human-bumped) and CFBundleVersion (build number, must monotonically increase). Plan: set MARKETING_VERSION to an honest pre-1.0 value in project.yml, auto-derive CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION from 'git rev-list --count HEAD' at build time via xcodebuild command-line override (no manual bookkeeping, no pbxproj/project.yml edits per build), and stamp the git short SHA into Info.plist (GitCommitSHA key, also via command-line override + $(GIT_COMMIT_SHA) expansion) so a distributed DMG can be traced to an exact commit. Surfaced in SettingsView so a tester can read it off directly. Steve: 'don't need to coordinate them to Git at the moment except maybe to embed a commit string in the package somewhere visible.'
notes:
Implementation:
- project.yml: MARKETING_VERSION 1.0 -> 0.1.0 on both targets (container app + widget). Added GIT_COMMIT_SHA build setting (default 'unknown').
- Both targets' Info.plist properties now explicitly set CFBundleShortVersionString: $(MARKETING_VERSION) and CFBundleVersion: $(CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION) as literal placeholder strings -- REQUIRED, not cosmetic: discovered xcodegen only bakes those two keys as literal values the FIRST time it creates an Info.plist, then leaves them alone on every later 'generate' since they aren't declared under properties. That's exactly how three ad-hoc builds all shipped reading a stale hardcoded '1.0'/'1' even though nothing was wrong with the settings themselves. Also added GitCommitSHA: $(GIT_COMMIT_SHA).
- Makefile: new GIT_SHA (short SHA, +'-dirty' suffix if the tree has uncommitted changes) and GIT_BUILD_NUMBER (git rev-list --count HEAD) variables; XCODEBUILD_VERSION_OVERRIDES passed on the command line to both app-build and app-package's xcodebuild invocations, so the build number/commit stamp are always fresh with zero manual bookkeeping.
- New AppVersionInfo.swift (BluegullAQI target): pure displayString(shortVersion:buildNumber:gitCommitSHA:) plus a Bundle.main-backed .current, defensively drops an unexpanded '$(GIT_COMMIT_SHA)' literal (raw Xcode build bypassing the Makefile).
- SettingsView: caption at the bottom showing e.g. 'v0.1.0 (171) · d5bd66a'.

Verified end-to-end: make app-build -> built Info.plist shows 0.1.0 / 171 / d5bd66a-dirty (dirty correctly flagged, tree had uncommitted changes at build time). codesign --verify passes on the app and widget. make test-swift green (added AppVersionInfoTests).
close_reason: Marketing version reset to 0.1.0, build number auto-derived from git commit count, git SHA stamped into Info.plist and shown in Settings. Verified the Info.plist actually reflects it after a real build -- the xcodegen stale-literal gotcha would have silently defeated this otherwise.

title: Verification plan for the helper (mostly not unit-testable)
description:
Most of this epic is OS-integration behaviour that unit tests can't reach -- launchd lifecycle, TCC grants, XPC Activity scheduling, background-item revocation. Needs a written manual verification script in the same spirit as bluegull-aqi-e70.8 and mtm.9.

At minimum: clean install first-run prompt count; helper refreshes with the app quit; helper exits when idle rather than lingering; toggling the background item off is detected and surfaced; reboot with no login (agent must NOT be login-scoped -- no RunAtLoad); widget shows fresh data after hours with the app never launched. The os_log instrumentation pattern from the spike (subsystem + category, streamed with log stream) worked well and should be kept in the shipping helper at .debug level.
acceptance_criteria: A documented manual verification checklist exists and has been run end to end on a real Mac at least once.

title: Degraded mode when the helper is disabled, unapproved, or absent
description:
Once the helper is the sole location owner, its absence must not brick current-location. Cases to handle: user switches the background item off in Login Items & Extensions (silent, at any time); SMAppService.status == .requiresApproval; registration failed; helper crashed.

Behaviour needs a decision but the likely shape: the app falls back to resolving location itself while it is running (it can, and it already holds a grant in the pre-helper world), and the popover explains why background refresh is off with a way to re-enable. Must interact correctly with e70.31 -- a stale reading still must not appear in the menu bar.
acceptance_criteria: With the background item switched off, the app still shows current AQI while running, tells the user background refresh is disabled, and offers a path to re-enable. No silent failure.

title: Make the helper the SOLE location owner (one grant, one fetcher)
description:
The helper is a separate bundle and therefore a separate TCC identity, so it needs its OWN location grant -- Apple sidesteps this with the private com.apple.locationd.effective_bundle, which we cannot use. Done naively that means the user sees TWO location prompts, app and helper, which is a bad first run.

Fix by inverting ownership: the helper becomes the only process that resolves GPS and fetches. The menu bar app and the widget both just READ the App Group cache, exactly as the widget already does. One grant, one fetcher, no duplicated AirNow calls, and it collapses to the architecture Steve originally sketched with the daemon as the boss.

Consequence to design deliberately: with the helper disabled or unapproved, nothing resolves location. The app needs a sensible degraded mode -- see the sibling fallback task.
acceptance_criteria: Exactly one location permission prompt across a clean install and first run. No AQI fetch originates from the app or the widget for the current-location case.

title: Schedule wakeups with XPC Activity rather than a timer
description:
Use xpc_activity_register for periodic refresh, mirroring com.apple.weatherd.notifications: GracePeriod ~900s, AllowBattery, RequireNetworkConnectivity, Priority Utility. The system then picks a moment when running is cheap, instead of us holding a wall-clock timer and waking the machine on our own schedule.

This is also the direct answer to Steve's standing concern about wasting AirNow queries refreshing data nobody is looking at: a grace period lets the OS coalesce our work with other activity, and the existing backend already bounds upstream load anyway (grid-snapped to ~1.1km via cache.LOCATION_KEY_PRECISION=2, hour-aligned TTLs, 400 cache-miss budget/hour), so AirNow load scales with populated grid cells rather than user count.
acceptance_criteria: Helper refreshes on a system-scheduled cadence with no timer of its own, and does not keep the machine awake. Cadence sanity-checked against AirNow's roughly-hourly NowCast publish rate.

title: Helper resolves location, fetches, and writes the App Group cache
description:
The actual job. On wake: resolve GPS, fetch AQI via the current DataSourceMode, write the reading into the shared App Group cache (including the aqi-cache-current-location slot), then end its transaction so launchd can reap it.

Reuse BluegullAQIKit wholesale -- AQIFetchCoordinator, AppGroupCache, DataSourceModeStore, LocationResolver all already work in a non-app process (the spike proved a plain helper gets CoreLocation fine).

FIX A LATENT BUG WHILE HERE: SystemLocationProvider.currentLocation() (LocationResolver.swift:82) reads manager.authorizationStatus synchronously microseconds after constructing CLLocationManager and throws .permissionDenied on .notDetermined. That is a real CoreLocation race -- the status isn't populated until the manager round-trips with locationd. A long-lived app never notices; a short-lived helper woken by launchd absolutely can. Wait for locationManagerDidChangeAuthorization before judging the status.
acceptance_criteria: With the menu bar app not running, a wake cycle refreshes the current-location cache entry, and a Current Location widget shows fresh data on its next timeline. Verified by quitting the app, clearing the slot, and observing the helper repopulate it.

title: Register/unregister the helper via SMAppService.agent, and handle revocation
description:
Container app registers the agent on first launch (the widget extension cannot -- app extensions cannot spawn processes or call SMAppService, which is why 'first widget starts the daemon' was never possible).

LaunchAgent plist modelled on com.apple.weatherd.plist: MachServices, EnablePressuredExit=true, EnableTransactions=true, ProcessType=Adaptive, and deliberately NO RunAtLoad and NO KeepAlive, so it is on-demand rather than login-scoped. This is what makes 'not started at login' achievable, which was Steve's explicit requirement.

REVOCATION IS THE NASTY PART: an SMAppService background item is enabled by default and appears in System Settings > General > Login Items & Extensions, where the user can switch it off at any time. The agent then silently stops and the app has no event for it -- failure is invisible and deferred, which is strictly worse than a denied prompt that fails loudly at a moment the user understands. Poll SMAppService.status for .requiresApproval and surface it in the popover.
acceptance_criteria: Agent registers on first launch and appears in Login Items & Extensions. Toggling it off is detected via SMAppService.status and surfaced to the user rather than failing silently. Unregisters cleanly on uninstall.

title: Scaffold helper agent target with a FRESH bundle id
description:
New LSUIElement, sandboxed helper target embedded in the app at Contents/Library/LaunchAgents (or Contents/MacOS for an SMAppService.agent program), signed with team G5DWPBWHQ5.

CRITICAL: do NOT reuse the bundle id 'solutions.bluegull.aqi.helper'. The 2026-08-12 spike left a real, still-present locationd grant for that identifier in /var/db/locationd/clients.plist (Authorized=true, pinned to that bundle id plus Steve's 'Apple Development: Steven Barber' leaf cert). It could not be removed -- tccutil has no authority over locationd-managed Location grants and fails with -10814 -- so a helper reusing that id would silently inherit a location grant, skip the first-run prompt, mask a real bug, and make any test of the genuine first-run experience invalid. Use something distinct, e.g. solutions.bluegull.aqi.locationhelper.

Entitlements needed (all public): com.apple.security.app-sandbox, com.apple.security.personal-information.location, com.apple.security.network.client, and the shared App Group group.solutions.bluegull.aqi. Keychain access group too if the helper does Direct-mode fetches.
acceptance_criteria: Helper builds, signs, launches, and writes a recognisable line to os_log. Bundle id is new and confirmed absent from /var/db/locationd/clients.plist before first run.

title: [epic] Location helper agent: background refresh without the menu bar app
description:
Give BlueGull AQI an always-available background process that owns location resolution and AQI fetching, so 'Current Location' widgets stay fresh whether or not the menu bar app is running.

WHY THIS EXISTS (all empirically established 2026-08-11/12, branch spike/widget-location):

1. A macOS widget extension CANNOT resolve location. Proven across three spike rounds with every precondition satisfied -- com.apple.security.personal-information.location on the extension, WhenInUse + both Always usage-description keys in the extension's OWN Info.plist, container app at authorizedAlways, and the system itself reporting isAuthorizedForWidgetUpdates=TRUE in the app. The extension still reported authStatus=0/notDetermined with delegateCallbacks=0: CoreLocation never engages with it at all.

2. Apple's own Weather widget does resolve location -- via com.apple.locationd.effective_bundle ('attribute my requests to my containing app's bundle'), a PRIVATE entitlement present on WeatherWidget.appex, WeatherMenu.app and weatherd alike. Third parties cannot use it. So there is no configuration we missed; the inheritance mechanism is simply not available to us.

3. A separate helper bundle CAN resolve location, including headless under launchd. Verified with a minimal signed sandboxed LSUIElement helper: user-launched it prompted and got a fix (41m); launchd-started with the grant already in place it got a fix with NO prompt and no user present (35m).

NET: pinned-location widgets are already self-sufficient (mtm.24) and unaffected. Current Location structurally requires another process. This epic is that process. Whether to build it at all is bluegull-aqi-hib.1.
design: Model on Apple's weatherd (/System/Library/LaunchAgents/com.apple.weatherd.plist), whose entire lifecycle is public API: MachServices + EnablePressuredExit + EnableTransactions + XPC Activity scheduling, with NO RunAtLoad and NO KeepAlive. That is exactly the 'starts when needed, exits when nobody is using it' shape Steve originally described -- my earlier claim that it was infeasible was wrong about launchd and right only about the narrower point that a widget extension cannot START anything. Registration is via SMAppService.agent from the container app on first launch.

title: Widget: show absolute date/time of the reading, never relative 'X hours ago'
description:
Steve's requirement (2026-08-11), stated directly: 'If the data is more than an hour old, I want the widget to say the date and time the data is from. I dislike X hours ago as being vague.'

Today BluegullAQIWidgetView.staleCaption (BluegullAQIWidgetView.swift, ~line 106) formats with RelativeDateTimeFormatter and renders exactly the disliked string -- Steve's own screenshot this morning read 'Last updated 3 hours ago'. Replace with the absolute local date/time the observation is from.

Boundary: 'more than an hour old' maps cleanly onto AppGroupCache.defaultSoftTTL = 3600 (the existing soft/stale threshold); defaultHardTTL is 3*3600. Under an hour, no timestamp is needed.

Applies to BOTH places the widget can express data age: (a) staleCaption's existing no-reading-but-fetched-before case, and (b) the present-but-stale case bluegull-aqi-dc2.6 will add -- dc2.6 should adopt this format rather than inventing a relative one.
design: Prefer the observation's own dateObserved/hourObserved/localTimeZone (which AirNow supplies and AQIReading already carries) over the fetch timestamp where possible -- Steve asked for 'the date and time the data is from', which is the observation time, not when we happened to retrieve it. Note the existing entry.date-relative formatting was chosen for mtm.11 golden-image snapshot determinism; an absolute timestamp derived from fixed fixture data is MORE deterministic, so this simplifies that constraint rather than fighting it. Rendering changes require re-recording snapshots (make record-snapshots), which Steve reviews per the Makefile's documented workflow.
acceptance_criteria: A widget whose data is over an hour old displays the absolute local date and time the reading is from. No surface renders relative phrasing like 'X hours ago'. Golden snapshots re-recorded and reviewed.
notes: DECIDED by Steve 2026-08-12: use the OBSERVATION time, not the fetch time -- 'the date and time the data is from' means when the air was measured. Source it from AirNow's dateObserved/hourObserved/localTimeZone, which AQIReading already carries; do NOT use AppGroupCache.lastSuccessfulFetchDate, which can overstate freshness by an hour or more. Rendered format e.g. 'Observed Tue Aug 12, 5:00 PM EDT'. Show it once the reading is older than the 1h soft TTL (AppGroupCache.defaultSoftTTL).
close_reason: Implemented in dc1f62f: absolute observation timestamps on widget staleCaption, menu bar never renders soft/hard-expired readings

title: API key field: don't auto-focus by default; disable when AirNow direct isn't selected
description:
Steve's user feedback (2026-08-11), two related fixes to AirNowAPIKeyEntryView.swift (mac-app/BluegullAQI):
1. The API key SecureField (line 28) currently has no explicit focus management, so it's likely getting default first-responder focus when the Settings tab opens. Wants focus to land somewhere else by default.
2. The field currently has no .disabled() modifier and doesn't even receive the current DataSourceMode, so it accepts input regardless of which data source is selected. Wants it disabled (non-editable) whenever AirNow direct isn't the selected data source (i.e. enabled only in Direct mode, matching DataSourceModeToggle.swift's mode) -- since the key is irrelevant/unused in Service mode.

Updated BluegullAQIUITests: testAirNowAPIKeyEntryFlow now switches to Direct mode first; added testAPIKeyFieldDisabledOutsideDirectMode. Verified via xcodebuild build (BUILD SUCCEEDED).

title: Real app icon + create-dmg polished DMG packaging
description: The app currently ships with Xcode's default gray icon (no Assets.xcassets existed), and make app-package's DMG step is a bare 'hdiutil create -srcfolder' -- functional but plain: no custom volume icon, no background art, no Applications drop-link, arbitrary window size. The supplied 'rounded_square' 1024 master had actual white pixels filled into its corners (not transparent) rather than being a true full-bleed square -- wrong shape for a macOS AppIcon source, which the OS masks into its own squircle itself; feeding it a pre-rounded image would double-mask and leave visible artifacts. Flood-filled those corners with the background blue to produce a genuine full-bleed 1024 master before deriving the iconset from it.
acceptance_criteria: mac-app/BluegullAQI/Assets.xcassets/AppIcon.appiconset has all 10 standard macOS icon sizes generated from a full-bleed (not pre-rounded) 1024 master, wired via ASSETCATALOG_COMPILER_APPICON_NAME so a real signed build shows the BlueGull gull icon in Finder/Dock/About. make app-package uses create-dmg with a custom volume icon, branded background image, reasonable window size, and an --app-drop-link Applications shortcut -- verified by actually opening the resulting DMG and confirming the layout looks right, not just that the make target exits 0.
close_reason:

title: Adopt soft/hard TTL (stale-while-revalidate) in AppGroupCache
description:
From Steve's 2026-08-05 design doc section 11, approved for inclusion. Today AppGroupCache has a single 1-hour TTL: past it, get() returns nil and the surface shows 'Data Unavailable' while blocking on a fetch. Measured 2026-08-05, a real expired-entry refetch took 2.826s (Marlton -- backend cache miss requiring an upstream AirNow round trip), during which the widget showed nothing despite having a perfectly usable 1-hour-old reading.

Proposed values, deliberately NOT the doc's 10min/30min: soft = 1 hour (matches AirNow's own hourly update cadence and preserves current request volume -- 10 minutes would multiply it 6x against a rate-limited API), hard = 3 hours (fallback window, past which data is too old to show).

NOTE: AQICacheEntry is Codable and persisted, so adding fields means existing cached entries won't decode. AppGroupCache already treats undecodable entries as junk and sweeps them, so the cost is one refetch per location after update -- acceptable for a cache.
acceptance_criteria: A soft-expired entry renders immediately and revalidates in the background rather than blocking; a hard-expired entry does not render. Freshness is surfaced so the UI can distinguish fresh from stale. Existing AppGroupCache tests updated; new tests cover both thresholds.
close_reason:
Implemented, partially -- the mechanical cache behavior and data-layer freshness are done and tested; a visual staleness indicator is deliberately split into bluegull-aqi-dc2.6 rather than pushed as an unreviewed golden-snapshot change (see that bead).

AQICacheEntry now carries softExpiresAt/hardExpiresAt (was one expiresAt) plus AQIFreshness (.fresh/.stale/.expired) and freshness(at:). AppGroupCache.get()/getCurrentLocation() now return a reading through the stale window, only going nil past the hard threshold -- previously they went nil at the single TTL, which is what produced the 2.826s blocking-fetch case measured for Marlton in bluegull-aqi-mtm.23. Added freshness(for:)/currentLocationFreshness()/mostRecentEntryFreshness(), all nil past hard expiry (a real bug in my own first pass -- they returned .expired instead of nil, caught by testCurrentLocationFreshnessMirrorsGetCurrentLocation failing). Defaults: soft=1hr (AirNow's own cadence, matches the pre-existing single TTL so request volume is unchanged), hard=3hr (fallback window). WidgetTimelineSnapshot/BluegullAQIWidgetEntry now carry freshness end-to-end using the same location-specified-vs-fallback cascade shape as reading itself.

Deliberately NOT implemented: active background revalidation of a stale entry. The widget only fetches when reading is nil (absent or hard-expired); a stale-but-present entry is returned as-is with no refetch triggered from the widget process. This is an accepted, disclosed gap, not an oversight -- a fire-and-forget Task in the widget extension is unreliable (the process can be suspended immediately after returning its Timeline, per doc/DESIGN.md ​4.3's own documented constraint), and rebuilding a proactive revalidation loop in the container app would partially undo bluegull-aqi-mtm.24's cleanup from earlier today. In practice: the menu bar's own displayed location still revalidates every runLoop cycle (~hourly) regardless; other locations only a widget looks at stay visibly-aged until something else re-fetches them (a hard expiry blocking-fetch, or coincidental other traffic).

184 BluegullAQIKit tests (12 new: 5 AQICacheEntryTests, 6 AppGroupCacheTests, 3 WidgetTimelineComputerTests -- net count differs slightly from raw additions since two pre-existing tests needed fixing for the new signature, described below) + 11 BluegullAQITests pass. Caught and fixed two of my own test bugs along the way: several 'force full expiry' tests set only hardTTL via a mechanical find-replace, leaving softTTL at its 3600s default -- since freshness() checks soft first, entries never actually reached .expired. And one new test wrote a cache entry under an unrounded location key while currentSnapshot(for:) correctly looks up the rounded one, the same class of bug as bluegull-aqi-nmn, just in a test rather than production code this time.

title: Large widget AQI number doesn't scale with Dynamic Type; accessibility snapshot test can never fail
description:
Discovered while showing widget screenshots: large-typical-accessibility-dynamic-type.png is byte-for-byte identical (same MD5) to large-typical.png. The snapshot test (BluegullAQIWidgetSnapshotTests.swift:122-123) applies .environment(\.dynamicTypeSize, .accessibility3) before rendering, but the resulting image is 100% unchanged from the non-accessibility variant -- not just the fixed-size number, the ENTIRE render, suggesting the environment override isn't propagating through the ImageRenderer harness at all, not only affecting the one hardcoded font.

Two distinct problems:
1. Accessibility gap: the headline AQI number in LargeWidgetLayout uses a fixed-size font (BluegullAQIWidgetView.swift:175, .font(.system(size: 32, weight: .semibold, design: .rounded))) instead of a Dynamic-Type-aware semantic style, unlike .subheadline/.caption used elsewhere in the same view. Users with larger text accessibility settings get no benefit for the most prominent element in the widget.
2. Test coverage gap: the accessibility snapshot test can never fail regardless of what changes, since its golden image is identical to a different test's golden image -- it provides zero actual regression coverage today.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Root-cause why .environment(\.dynamicTypeSize, ...) doesn't visibly affect the ImageRenderer output at all (harness issue vs. WidgetKit/ImageRenderer platform limitation). 2. If it's fixable, make the large AQI number scale appropriately with Dynamic Type (or document why WidgetKit widgets deliberately don't support it, if that's a real platform constraint). 3. The accessibility snapshot test's golden image must differ from large-typical.png once fixed, so it's actually exercising something.
close_reason: Root-caused: ImageRenderer does not honor .environment(\.dynamicTypeSize, ...) at all on this platform -- confirmed via an isolated repro independent of this codebase (bare Text().font(.caption) renders byte-identical regardless of the override; colorScheme override on the same pipeline works fine, per testLargeTypicalDarkMode). Fixed the real accessibility gap anyway: small/medium/large widget layouts now use @ScaledMetric instead of a fixed .system(size:) font for the headline AQI number, so it correctly scales on a real widget host even though our headless harness can't verify it. Removed the misleading testLargeTypicalAccessibilityDynamicType snapshot test (could never fail -- its golden image was always identical to large-typical's) and its orphaned PNG, with a doc comment explaining why. title: Label displayed values as NowCast, not a spot reading
description:
AirNow's real-time observations are NowCast AQI -- EPA's endorsed method for relating short-term data to the AQI. It uses a VARIABLE averaging window: longer when air quality is stable, shorter when changing fast (PM2.5 ~12h stable / ~3h variable; ozone ~8h stable / ~1h variable).

So the number is a weighted average designed to track lived experience -- NOT an instantaneous sensor reading, and NOT the daily AQI (which requires a full 24 hours and is what agencies report for 'yesterday'). UI copy must not imply otherwise: avoid phrasing like 'right now' or 'current reading' that suggests a spot measurement.

'Current Air Quality' is the phrasing airnow.gov itself uses and is safe. This is a copy/labeling task, plus deciding whether to surface a brief explanation of NowCast somewhere reachable (natural fit alongside the preliminary-data disclaimer in the popover/expand view). See doc/DESIGN.md 'What the number is: NowCast, not a spot reading'.

title: Handle AQI > 500 (beyond the AQI scale) as valid data
description:
The category model currently has no representation for AQI above 500, so the default behavior is a blank/unknown category -- which would black out the app during exactly the conditions that produce such readings. That is the failure mode to design against.

RESOLVED: >500 is rare but REAL DATA, not an error.
  - TAD Table 1 bounds Hazardous at 301-500; above that is 'Beyond the AQI', where a value 'can still be computed to indicate relative magnitude' using the Hazardous breakpoints, and users should 'follow the recommendations for the Hazardous category'. NowCast handles it no differently. EPA would not document a computation for something that could only be a fault.
  - It has actually occurred in official reporting: Oregon DEQ recorded Bend above 500 on 2020-09-12 ('beyond the AQI scale' in their words), Newport 'well over 500', during that September's wildfires.
  - We never compute AQI (bluegull-aqi-10h.17), so anything received has already passed AirNow's own QA. Data trustworthiness is upstream of us; our obligation is to disseminate as received.

EARLIER ERROR CORRECTED: a previous version of this issue claimed airnow.gov diverged from the TAD by showing '301 +'. Wrong -- that came from a collapsed text extraction. The expanded AQI Legend panel shows '301 - 500  Hazardous' plus 'Values above 500 are beyond the AQI scale'. Both sources agree; there is no conflict to resolve.

IMPLEMENT: display the actual value; keep maroon (#7E0023) and the Hazardous health guidance per the TAD's explicit direction; indicate it is beyond the scale, using AirNow's own phrasing ('Values above 500 are beyond the AQI scale') rather than inventing wording. Do NOT clamp to 500 -- that would misrepresent the reading and conflicts with 'disseminated as received'.

SEPARATE CONCERN, handle distinctly: genuinely malformed values -- negative AQI, non-numeric, absurd magnitudes -- indicate a parse or transport fault rather than extreme air, and belong in an error state, not the beyond-the-scale path. Don't conflate the two.

Test with a fixture at e.g. AQI 650 to confirm it renders correctly rather than blanking.
close_reason: Fixed a real conflation bug: negative AQI (malformed data) previously fell through the same default case as >500 (real beyond-the-scale data), silently misclassifying corrupted input as extreme air quality. AQICategory.init(aqi:) is now failable, returning nil for negative input; PollutantReading.category updated to flatMap accordingly. Added isBeyondScale and beyondScaleNotice (AirNow's own verbatim phrasing 'Values above 500 are beyond the AQI scale', not invented wording). Deliberately did not add upper-bound implausibility detection -- disseminating AirNow's data as received (10h.17) means not second-guessing magnitude past the one unambiguous boundary (negative). Tested with AQI 650 (matching the real Oregon DEQ 2020 wildfire historical example cited in this issue) confirming it renders as valid data, not blank. 22/22 tests pass via swift test.

title: Bound App Group cache retention and review file protection
description: The App Group container holds the user's location history on disk -- the locations matter considerably more than the AQI values do. Bound retention rather than accumulating indefinitely, and review the file protection class on the container.
close_reason: Found a real gap: original AppGroupCache.get() treated an expired entry as a miss but never deleted it, so stale entries accumulated forever, and since cleanup only fired reactively on a get() for that exact key, a never-revisited location would never get cleaned up. Fixed with two mechanisms: (1) expired entries deleted both reactively on get() and proactively across every entry on each put(). (2) hard cap on entry count (maxRetainedEntries=10), evicting oldest-by-fetchedAt when exceeded -- TTL alone only bounds age not count. Added SharedCacheStore.allKeys() so AppGroupCache can enumerate/sweep its own prefixed entries without touching a shared store's other data. File protection: verified against Apple's own Security Guide that macOS has no per-file Data Protection classes like iOS -- Class A is backed by the FileVault volume key on macOS, Class D is unsupported. No per-file protection-class API applies here; documented this conclusion in the doc comment rather than leaving it silently unaddressed. Verified against both the in-memory fake and real UserDefaults. 68/68 tests pass.

title: Add jittered refresh scheduling to client
description: Hourly refresh means every install would otherwise wake at the top of the hour and synchronize into a server-side spike. Each install derives a stable offset within the hour from a per-install value -- stable rather than re-randomized each refresh, so the interval stays consistent -- spreading load uniformly. Directly reduces peak load on the backend.
close_reason: RefreshScheduler derives a stable per-install offset within the refresh interval (persisted via SharedCacheStore, so container app and widget see the same schedule) and computes the next refresh time on that install's interval-spaced schedule -- spreading load across installs instead of everyone waking at the top of the hour. Offset generated once and persisted, not regenerated per call. Found and fixed a real floating-point precision bug via testing: Date stores time relative to 2001 not 1970, so converting large 'seconds since 1970' values loses low-order precision, making a raw-Double 'strictly after now' check fail intermittently near computed boundaries. Root-caused with an isolated repro script, fixed by doing the strictly-after check and any bump entirely in Date's own domain rather than mixing pre/post-conversion Double representations. Verified with 30 consecutive runs of the specific test, then 3 full-suite runs. 75/75 tests pass via swift test.
